transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I guess what finally made me come in is... I keep turning in these applications and research notes with these small, just really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll completely mislabel an artwork date. 

Which actually happened the other day with this Goya piece. I don't know if you're into art history at all, but his Black Paintings are just... they're so intense. I actually went down this huge rabbit hole last night reading about the house he painted them in—the Quinta del Sordo—and how they had to transfer the murals to canvas years later. It's wild how they even do that without ruining the plaster, honestly. I was watching this whole documentary on art restoration instead of sleeping. 

But, um, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, so I'll mess up a date like that, or I'll just completely skip a question on an application. And the worst part is, I honestly thought I had checked them. Like, I swear I'll sit there and look over the whole page, but I still miss it somehow.
Have you had these kinds of attention or careless mistakes since you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I had really good ideas, but I'd just... forget to turn in the actual worksheets. Or I'd completely lose the instructions for projects. 

Like, in fourth grade, we had this diorama project on the solar system, and I spent hours painting these styrofoam balls. I used this really cool glow-in-the-dark paint for Jupiter, which, I mean, Jupiter doesn't even glow, but I thought it looked amazing in my room at night. I even mixed different shades of orange and red for the Great Red Spot, and I accidentally got paint all over my mom's carpet. She was so mad, we had to put a rug over that stain for like three years before they finally replaced the flooring. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. Yeah, I completely lost the rubric for that project. I was always missing little details like that, or losing my homework, unless my parents physically checked my backpack every single night. If they didn't go through it, things just vanished. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one part of your life, like at work or school and also at home?

Um, yeah, I'd say so. It's definitely not just a school thing. Like, at home, my apartment is... well, it's a bit of a disaster area right now. I'll start doing the dishes, and then I'll notice the sponge is looking kind of gross, so I'll go to the cabinet to get a new one. But then I'll see that the cabinet is completely disorganized, and I'll start pulling everything out to rearrange the cleaning supplies. 

Which, actually, I found this amazing all-natural cleaner the other day. It smells like eucalyptus and mint, and it's supposed to be super safe for pets, not that I have a pet, but I really want a cat. I was looking at the local shelter's website, and they have this beautiful orange tabby named Marmalade. I grew up with an orange cat, and they just have the best personalities, you know? They're always so goofy. 

But, um, wait. What were we talking about? Oh, right, my apartment. Yeah, so I'll start organizing the cabinet, and then three hours later, the dishes are still in the sink, the cabinet is empty, and I'm on the floor reading an old magazine I found shoved in the back. So, yeah, it definitely happens at home too. My roommates get pretty frustrated with me sometimes.
Do you often feel excessively worried or on edge most days?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm constantly worried or anything like that. I'm actually pretty laid back most of the time. Sometimes a little too laid back, I guess, if you ask my parents. 

They're always telling me I need to take things more seriously, especially now that I'm done with my bachelor's. My dad actually just retired last month, and he's been spending all his time building these intricate birdhouses in the garage. He made this one that looks exactly like a miniature Victorian mansion, with little shingles and everything. It's crazy how much detail he puts into them. He even ordered these tiny brass hinges for the doors from some specialty shop in England. I think he's trying to get me to help him with them, but I just don't have the patience for all those tiny pieces. 

But, uh, what was the question? Oh, right, feeling on edge. Yeah, no, I don't really get anxious or worried like that on a day-to-day basis. Just mostly frustrated with myself for messing things up, you know?
Do you often fidget or feel like you need to move around when you’re expected to sit still?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have to get up and run around or anything. I can sit still fine. Like, I go to the movies all the time and I never have a problem sitting through them. 

Actually, I just saw that new sci-fi movie that came out last weekend. The one with the time travel? It was so good. The special effects were incredible, especially the part where they go back to the dinosaur era. I've always been obsessed with dinosaurs. When I was a kid, I wanted to be a paleontologist. I had this huge collection of plastic dinosaurs, and I would bury them in the sandbox in our backyard and pretend I was digging up real fossils. My mom got so mad because I'd track sand all over the house. She ended up getting me this little brush thing to dust myself off before I came inside, but I always forgot to use it. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, fidgeting. Right. Yeah, no, I don't really have a problem sitting still. I might bounce my leg a little bit sometimes if I'm bored, but it's not like I feel this crazy urge to get up and move around.
Do these attention and organization problems cause problems in your daily life?

Um, yeah, they definitely do. It's been pretty frustrating lately, actually. Because of all this, I've ended up submitting work late, and I even missed a couple of important application deadlines for grad school. 

Which really sucks because I spent so much time researching programs. I found this one in Colorado that looked amazing. It's right near the mountains, and I've always wanted to learn how to snowboard. My buddy went out there last winter and said the powder is just incredible. He brought back this really cool artisanal hot sauce from a local farmer's market there. It was made with ghost peppers, and I swear, I put just a tiny drop on my eggs and my mouth was on fire for like twenty minutes. I had to drink half a gallon of milk just to calm it down. I don't even know how people can eat stuff that spicy on a regular basis. 

But, um, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the problems it causes. Yeah, so missing those deadlines was bad. And I actually had a mentor tell me recently that my lack of follow-through is starting to hurt opportunities that I really should be ready for at this point. So, yeah, it's definitely causing some real issues for me.
Before age 12, did you already have these attention or organization problems at school or home?

Yeah, for sure. Even back in elementary school, it was kind of a thing. My teachers would always write on my report cards that I had really good ideas, but I'd always forget to turn in my worksheets or I'd lose the instructions. 

I remember one time in fourth grade, we had to do this big project on the solar system, and I spent hours building this really cool papier-mâché model of Jupiter. I even mixed different colors of paint to get the Great Red Spot just right. I used this really specific shade of crimson that I found in my mom's craft supplies. She used to do all this scrapbooking back then, with these fancy textured papers and little metal brads. She had this whole dedicated room for it with shelves full of different colored ribbons. I used to go in there and just look at all the different patterns. She made this huge album for my grandparents' 50th anniversary that took her like six months to finish. 

Wait, what was I... oh, right, school when I was younger. Yeah, so I'd miss little details all the time. Honestly, the only way I got through was because my parents would check my backpack every single night to make sure I actually had my homework and hadn't lost anything important.
When you were a child, did teachers or parents ever describe you as overly active or constantly 'on the go'?

Um, no, not really. I don't think anyone ever said I was hyper or anything like that. I was actually pretty quiet as a kid. I spent a lot of time just reading or drawing. I loved drawing cars, especially vintage ones. My grandpa had this old '67 Mustang that he kept in his garage. It was this gorgeous cherry red color, and he would spend every Sunday morning waxing it. He'd turn on the radio, usually some old Motown station, and just polish that car for hours. Sometimes he'd let me help, but mostly I just sat on a stool and watched him. He used this specific type of carnauba wax that smelled like coconuts. Every time I smell coconut now, it reminds me of his garage. 

He actually promised he'd teach me how to drive it when I turned sixteen, but then the transmission went out and he never got around to fixing it. It just sat there under a tarp for years. It's kind of sad, really. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Being active? Yeah, no, I wasn't really the running around type. I was pretty chill, just, you know, in my own world most of the time.
Do you also have these attention or organization problems at work or in other adult responsibilities, not just at home?

Um, well, I actually don't have a job right now, so I can't really say for work. I've been looking, though. I actually had an interview last week at this really cool indie coffee shop downtown. They roast all their own beans right there in the store. They have this massive, shiny brass roasting machine right behind the counter, it looks almost like something out of a steampunk movie. The owner was telling me they get their beans from this specific farm in Ethiopia, and apparently, the altitude there makes the coffee naturally taste like blueberries. Which sounds totally fake, right? But he gave me a sample, and it actually did. It was wild. 

I ended up buying a bag for my roommate because he's obsessed with pour-over coffee. He has this whole elaborate morning ritual with a special gooseneck kettle and a little digital scale. It takes him like fifteen minutes just to make one cup. I usually just drink instant or grab an energy drink because I don't have the patience to measure out water by the gram. 

But, uh... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, adult responsibilities and work. Yeah, so since I'm not working right now, I haven't really had a chance to mess anything up there. And with other adult stuff, I don't know, I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed it outside of what happens with my classes and just my normal stuff at home.
Do you often interrupt other people or blurt out answers before a question is finished?

No, I don't think I do that. I actually really hate when people do that. My friend Josh is super bad about it. Like, we were playing this new board game the other night—it's one of those strategy games with all the little wooden train cars? Ticket to Ride, I think it's called. It's a really fun game, you have to build these railway routes across the country. But the pieces are so tiny, and my cat kept jumping on the table trying to bat them off. He’s this big orange tabby, completely insane. We found him in a cardboard box behind a Wendy's when he was a kitten, and he still goes absolutely crazy whenever anyone brings home fast food. He'll literally try to tear into the paper bag to get at the french fries. It's hilarious but also kind of annoying when you're just trying to eat in peace. 

Anyway, Josh was there and he... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, interrupting people. Yeah, no, I'm usually pretty quiet in conversations. I mostly just listen and wait my turn, so I don't really blurt things out or talk over anyone.
When you were growing up, were there any concerns that you were slower than other kids in learning, understanding, or general development?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, my parents never said anything like that. I actually really liked school when I was little, especially the science stuff. We had this one teacher in third grade, Mr. Henderson, who brought in an incubator and we hatched baby chicks right there in the classroom. It was the coolest thing. We got to watch them peck their way out of the shells, and then we kept them in this big plastic tub with a heat lamp for a couple of weeks. One of them was a little smaller than the rest, and I named him Pip. He was mostly yellow but had this tiny black spot on his wing. I begged my mom to let me take him home when the project was over, but we lived in an apartment, so she said absolutely not. She was really strict about pets. The only thing she ever let me have was a goldfish, and it died after like three days because I accidentally overfed it. I dumped an entire container of those little flakes into the bowl because I thought he looked hungry. 

But, uh, wait, what were you asking? Slower at learning? Yeah, no, I did fine. I learned to read and do math and all that stuff right along with everyone else. Nobody ever seemed worried about it.
Do you still have these attention or organization problems in your current adult life, even outside of school?

Um, well, like I said earlier, I'm not really working right now, so I don't have that to go on. And outside of school stuff... I mean, I don't really think so? I mostly just hang out or play video games when I'm not doing schoolwork. I just got this new open-world RPG that is insanely huge. You can spend hours just wandering around picking herbs and crafting potions. I spent like four hours yesterday just trying to find this one specific type of glowing mushroom for a side quest. It only spawns in these caves at night in the game, but the day-night cycle is so slow, so I ended up just leaving my character standing in the cave while I went to make a sandwich. 

I make really good grilled cheese, by the way. The trick is to use mayo on the outside of the bread instead of butter. It sounds weird, but it makes it perfectly crispy without burning. My roommate thought I was crazy the first time he saw me do it, but now he asks me to make them for him all the time. We actually ran out of bread yesterday, so I had to walk to the bodega down the street. It was pouring rain, and I forgot my umbrella, so I was completely soaked by the time I got back. 

But, uh... what was the question again? Oh, right, adult life and organization. Yeah, no, I don't really have a lot of big adult responsibilities right now besides school, so I haven't really noticed any major problems with that kind of stuff. Just the normal school things I mentioned before.
When you were learning to read or do math as a child, did you have unusual difficulty compared with other kids?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, like I was saying about Mr. Henderson's class, I always did pretty okay with reading and math. Actually, reading was my favorite, mostly because we had this reading program where if you read a certain number of books, you got a coupon for a free personal pan pizza at Pizza Hut. The Book It program, I think it was called? I used to read so many of those Goosebumps books just to get the pizza. I had this huge stack of them in my room. The one with the ventriloquist dummy—Slappy, I think his name was—that one terrified me. I actually had to hide it under my bed because the cover creeped me out so much when I was trying to sleep. My brother found it once and put it in my closet just to mess with me, and I screamed so loud my dad came running upstairs thinking I was hurt. My brother got grounded for a week for that, which was kind of awesome because it meant I got to play the Super Nintendo by myself all weekend without him hogging the controller. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, learning to read and do math. Yeah, no, I didn't have any unusual problems with it. I just did it like everyone else did.

patient.answer:
Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, my parents never said anything like that. I actually really liked school when I was little, especially the science stuff. We had this one teacher in third grade, Mr. Henderson, who brought in an incubator and we hatched baby chicks right there in the classroom. It was the coolest thing. We got to watch them peck their way out of the shells, and then we kept them in this big plastic tub with a heat lamp for a couple of weeks. One of them was a little smaller than the rest, and I named him Pip. He was mostly yellow but had this tiny black spot on his wing. I begged my mom to let me take him home when the project was over, but we lived in an apartment, so she said absolutely not. She was really strict about pets. The only thing she ever let me have was a goldfish, and it died after like three days because I accidentally overfed it. I dumped an entire container of those little flakes into the bowl because I thought he looked hungry. 

But, uh, wait, what were you asking? Slower at learning? Yeah, no, I did fine. I learned to read and do math and all that stuff right along with everyone else. Nobody ever seemed worried about it.
